findings.title: Rows repeated exactly
findings.detail: 12 rows are exact copies of another row.
findings.impact: Every count and total from this file is overstated until copies are removed.

findings.title: The same ID appears on different rows
findings.detail: 5 order_id values appear on rows with different contents.
findings.impact: These are not simple copies: one of each pair is probably an edit or a mistake, and someone has to decide which row is right.

findings.title: More than one currency in the same column
findings.impact: Totals would add different currencies together. Each value needs converting to one currency (with the rate and date used) before any sum.

findings.title: Blank, padded or repeated column names
findings.detail: 1 header was renamed so every column has a usable name.
findings.impact: Repeated names usually mean two different fields share a label; someone who knows the export should say which is which.

findings.title: The same email address in different capitalisation
findings.detail: 1 address appears in different letter case.
findings.impact: These are almost certainly the same person counted as separate customers.

findings.title: Names that look like the same record
findings.detail: 1 pair of name values is nearly identical.
findings.impact: Likely typos or re-entered records; counts of unique customers or clients will be too high until they are merged.

findings.title: Negative values where amounts are expected
findings.impact: Often refunds or corrections. Totals are right only if that is intended; averages and counts of sales are not.

findings.title: Numbers stored with currency symbols or separators
findings.detail: 189 values include symbols or thousands separators.
findings.impact: Spreadsheets and databases read these as text, so they drop out of sums and averages unless they are cleaned first.

findings.title: Unusually large or small values
findings.detail: 5 values sit far outside the typical range (33.41 to 63.27 for the middle half).
findings.impact: Could be real (a big order) or an entry error (an extra zero). Averages will be pulled toward them either way; worth confirming.

findings.title: The same label is spelled several ways
findings.detail: 1 label differs only by case or spacing.
findings.impact: Breakdowns will split one group into several (e.g. 'US' and 'us ' counted separately).

findings.title: Missing values written as text
findings.detail: 8 cells hold placeholders instead of being empty.
findings.impact: Tools will treat these as real values: counts of distinct values and joins on this column will be wrong until they are blanked.

findings.title: Values with no match in customers
findings.detail: 6 customer_id values do not exist in customers.customer_id.
findings.impact: Rows with these values drop out of any report that joins the two files, usually because the reference list is out of date.

findings.title: Dates after the export date
findings.impact: Usually typos in the year or scheduled items mixed in with actuals; they land in the wrong period in any time series.

findings.title: Dates are written in more than one format
findings.impact: Dates like 03/04/2024 are ambiguous (March 4 or April 3), and sorting or monthly totals will be wrong until one format is used.

findings.title: Numbers stored with currency symbols or separators
findings.detail: 40 values include symbols or thousands separators.
findings.impact: Spreadsheets and databases read these as text, so they drop out of sums and averages unless they are cleaned first.

findings.title: Columns with no data
findings.impact: Safe to drop, unless the field was expected to be filled.

findings.title: Title rows above the header
findings.detail: The header is on row 3; the rows above it were skipped.
findings.impact: Fine for this audit, but anything that assumes row 1 is the header will read the title as column names.

findings.title: Values with leading or trailing spaces
findings.impact: Invisible, but 'Leeds' and 'Leeds ' will not match in lookups or joins.
